messages.author: bcfb6bc9f75aae0f
messages.subject: rstan 2.8.0 seems to be out. And fucks me sideways... How can I solve ?
parts:
A routine update of my CRAN packages got me rstan 2.8.0 (and StanHeaders 2.8.0), which is (yet) unannunced. And I'm fucked...

I used to dump the traceplots of my MCMC run on a multipage PDF with something along the lines of :

    PN <- F1@model_pars
    SLPN <- c("mu", "sigma", "rho", "delta")
    pdf(file="Check1-1.pdf", pointsize=12, width=7, height=10,
    paper="special", title="Charpentier - MCMC trace checking : study-level parameters")
    traceplot(F1, pars=SLPN, inc_warmup=FALSE, nrow=5, ncol=3)
    dev.off()

Those four parameters being (not so small) vectors (78 parameters total), I used to get a dense multipage PDF.

This worked up to rstan 2.7.0. rstan now uses ggplot2 to create a traceplot, which can be customized to death thanks to ggplot2 options. Nice (and commendable) idea...

But now, rstan::traceplot won't plot my 78 parameters on the 6 pages necessary for them. (And the interactive version (on screen) won't page me to pass to the next page...). It seems that I have to do that "by hand".

Nice regression when you have to submit a paper revision with a deadline...

Do you see a quick way to get rstan::traceplot to do that ?

By the way, the "ask=TRUE" option of the interactive version (probably inherited from coda's "traceplot") was a nice idea for interactive work. Could we get back something like that ?

--
Emmanuel Charpentier

parts:
I don't think that your language is appropriate --- Stan is an open
source project, you get to use it for free, bugs happen.

That said, a quick workaround could be installing an earlier version:
see, for example,

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/17082341/installing-older-version-of-r-package

or clone the git repo and check out the version with the relevant
earlier tag that worked for you.

Best,

Tamas

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan 2.8.0 seems to be out. And fucks me sideways... How can I solve ?
parts:
Hi Emmanuel,

Sorry for the annoyance. The switch to ggplot2 makes this a bit trickier, but you can do this with one loop using the pars argument to traceplot to select parameters you want on the same page and using the ggsave function inside the loop (the pdf function should probably work too instead of ggsave but I recommend ggsave).

rstan 2.8.0-1 should also be appearing on CRAN in a few days and I'll try to add an option before then that will automate this (e.g. by letting you just specify the number of parameters you want per page).

messages.author: bcfb6bc9f75aae0f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan 2.8.0 seems to be out. And fucks me sideways... How can I solve ?
parts:
Ahem... rstan 2.8.0 *IS* on CRAN. See the package page on CRAN , which says it has been published on Sep, 19. That's where I got it.

I managed to write a wrapper along the lines you suggested. An annoyance : ggplot2 seems to ignore the geometry when it can. Asking for five rows and three columns works, but if your last page has only three parameters, you'll get a last page with three columns and *one* line (the whole height of the page. Ugly...). Similarly, the size of the axes fonts needs adjusting (the default is way too large for the iteration numbers...). Small miseries, that "just" request to dive into ggplot2 docs. Ô joy...

HTH,

--
Emmanuel Charpentier

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan 2.8.0 seems to be out. And fucks me sideways... How can I solve ?
parts:
On Monday, September 21, 2015 at 10:22:46 AM UTC-4, Emmanuel Charpentier wrote:
Ahem... rstan 2.8.0 *IS* on CRAN. See the package page on CRAN , which says it has been published on Sep, 19. That's where I got it.
Yes, 2.8.0 is, but 2.8.0-1 is not.

I managed to write a wrapper along the lines you suggested. An annoyance : ggplot2 seems to ignore the geometry when it can. Asking for five rows and three columns works, but if your last page has only three parameters, you'll get a last page with three columns and *one* line (the whole height of the page. Ugly...). Similarly, the size of the axes fonts needs adjusting (the default is way too large for the iteration numbers...). Small miseries, that "just" request to dive into ggplot2 docs. Ô joy...

You've probably found this already, but all the fonts, axis tick marks, titles, etc. can be customized by adding theme elements (there are many examples if you look at help("theme", package = "ggplot2")). It's a bit strange at first if you're used to the base plotting functions in R, but once you get used to it there are a lot of advantages (of course there are some cases when ggplot makes things hard.) I was a slow convert to ggplot at first, but now I find that it takes me way longer to customize a base R plot than one made using ggplot. Just takes some practice.

As for package management for reproducibility, I second Mike Lawrence's suggestion of packrat. It's integrated with RStudio too, which makes it easier to use.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan 2.8.0 seems to be out. And fucks me sideways... How can I solve ?
parts:
It's actually not so easy to make it work out that way, although it would be nice.

rstan takes longer to get through the CRAN process than StanHeaders, but it can't go up in advance of StanHeaders because it requires StanHeaders. The CRAN process is also pretty standardized in that once StanHeaders makes it through, it's through, although the time until all binaries are built can vary. So StanHeaders would end up being available first even if the two were submitted at exactly the same time.
